learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected one-half and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Ran five-by-five grid at one-half: twenty-five remained, newcomers at most three neighbors but need four. Selecting three-eighths completed all 1521 in round51; two-fifths stalled25, quarter completed all in34, three-fifths stalled25 and needed five. Seven-by-seven at three-fifths and half stalled49. Line at half completed201 in100 rounds. Reset line returned two adopters; Step produced four.
observations.reveal: Corrected to three-eighths and explained three side neighbors, two near corner and one diagonal. Compared larger-block failure and successful line with one of two neighbors. Named cascade capacity. Prose said above three-eighths needs four, although three-fifths control had correctly required five.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Neighbor counts around block made boundary visible; line showed growing frontier. Finished-run table retained all comparisons. Some lower table content clipped during exploration, full table and explanation readable after reveal.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete neighbor rule and block support a meaningful threshold commitment.

interaction.reason: Multiple thresholds, larger seed, line topology and reset separate size from local geometry.
interaction.evidence: Grid three-eighths succeeds, half fails; line half succeeds.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects cascade limit to frontier neighbor counts.
payoff.evidence: Three of eight versus one of two.

clarity.reason: Neighbor numbers are strong; broad four-neighbor statement is imprecise for tested three-fifths.
clarity.evidence: Control required five at three-fifths, prose says above three-eighths needs four.

transfer.reason: Topology contrast generalizes within the same adoption model, no concrete external application.

accessibility.evidence: Text totals and finished-run table available; screen reader, keyboard, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: A larger starting block cannot beat local frontier limit.

visualExplanation.reason: Frontier neighbor counts directly expose mechanism.
visualExplanation.evidence: Side three, near corner two, corner one.

playfulness.reason: Threshold and topology controls invite many experiments.
playfulness.evidence: Five q values, two block sizes and line.

practicalValue.reason: Clarifies how network structure limits cascades.

depth.reason: Links discrete thresholds, topology and finite-seed propagation.
depth.evidence: Same fraction behaves differently across networks.

complexity.reason: Many controls support a nontrivial local-to-global cascade argument.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Convert fractional thresholds to integer neighbors and infer propagation from frontier geometry.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Run,step, five thresholds, size toggle, topology and reset controls.

whyCool: The frontier geometry can matter more than how large the initial crowd is.
caveat: Ideal regular networks and irreversible adoption only; above-threshold prose should say at least four rather than exactly four.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
